summary: The common-coset power completion (deg(R^r-F)<(r-1)D, Q=beta(R^r-F)) and the strict one-degree zero-avoidance extension re-derive correctly, the quadratic character-sum count is right, and the live counts (344 witnesses, 16 repair stages, 1934 proposals, 11 moves, 116319 Horner evaluations, 102->109 and 118->124/122) match the artifact. The tight strict counterexample at p5,N4,K2 is only valid for the square coset: the note does not say this, and with the nonresidue coset the constant Q=3 is a perfect strict solution. The header's list of what remains open names only K39, but the artifact's other mixed inputs are also unsolved and never reported in the text: r=3 N63,K46 (55/63, 56/63), r=4 N32,K24 (28/32, 27/32) and N31,K16 seed 71 (30/31). The norm attack it cites as superseding is quadratic-only and cannot reach the r=3/r=4 inputs. Nothing shown is wrong, so needs-work.

claims.quote: Thus ALL common-coset inputs are solved perfectly whenever K >= (r-1)*ceil(N/r)
claims.finding: Re-derived: F=W-T/beta has degree rD with r-th-power leading coefficient lambda^r, so the formal root exists (r | p-1, so r is invertible). R^r-F=E with deg E<(r-1)D, and Q=beta(R^r-F) agrees with t_i+beta R(a_i)^r because W(a_i)=0. With M=N this needs (r-1)ceil(N/r)<=K. The artifact's global inputs above threshold (N127,K77; N31,K16; r3 N63,K46; r4 N32,K24) are all perfect.

claims.quote: Hence K>=b+1 is a uniform sufficient condition for perfect STRICT common-coset completion
claims.step: Strict Nonzero Powers: Constructive Zero Avoidance
claims.finding: (R+c)^r-R^r has leading term r c R^(r-1) of degree (r-1)D=b, so deg Q_new<=b. The c values 0..M give M+1 distinct candidates (M<p) against at most M forbidden values -R(a_i). The strict siblings in the artifact use K=b+1 exactly where needed (r=4, N32 uses K25 rather than 24), and all ten strict controls are perfect.

claims.quote: At p5,N4,K2,r2, shifts(0,0,0,1), all25 native polynomials fail perfect strict satisfaction
claims.finding: The orientation is not stated, and the claim depends on it. Exhaustive recomputation: with beta=1 (square coset, the test's instance(...,29,global) has orientations (0,0,0,0)) no degree<2 polynomial works, which is correct. With the nonresidue coset beta=2, Q=3 gives residues 3,3,3,2, all nonzero nonsquares mod 5, so a perfect strict solution exists at K2. The counterexample therefore needs the condition 'common square coset'.

claims.quote: Including Z zeros, the accepted count is (p-chi(beta/beta_i)+Z)/2 >= (p-1)/2
claims.finding: sum_z chi(z^2+a/beta)=-1 for a!=0 gives n+ - n- = -chi(beta/beta_i) and n+ + n- + Z = p, so the accepted count n+ + Z = (p+Z-chi)/2 >= (p-1)/2. The success probability per proposal is at least 1/3 for p>=3. The degree bookkeeping h=max(0,2D-K+1), f=D-h+1 also checks: deg(2R0 L)<=2D-h<=K-1.

claims.quote: K39 and general fixed-input/asymptotic solvability remain open.
claims.finding: Omission in a summary of what is left open. In the artifact, the mixed inputs r=3 N63,K46 (best 55/63 and 56/63, the latter from the linear baseline), r=4 N32,K24 (28/32, 27/32) and N31,K16 seed 71 (30/31, NO_SAMPLED_IMPROVEMENT) are also unsolved. The text never reports the r=3/r=4 mixed scores at all: it states only that the common-coset controls are perfect. The superseding norm attack is quadratic-only and cannot apply to r=3/4, and at N31,K16 its budget K>max(|A|,D) cannot be met (it needs |A|+|B|<=29<31). The sixth configuration (p=65537, N16, K8) is also never named.

claims.quote: Live24-source artifact:16 repair stages,1934 retained proposals,11 accepted moves
claims.step: Adaptive Root-Value Exchange Is Now Executed
claims.finding: These match the artifact: 16 non-null repair records, 1934 proposals, 11 accepted moves and a sum of 116319 repair Horner evaluations. The N127,K39 mixed inputs go 102->109 for both seeds and N127,K77 mixed goes 118->124 and 118->122, all with NO_SAMPLED_IMPROVEMENT. The pass budgets equal N-initial+1 (26 and 10), as stated.

summary: The norm criterion, the degree budget K>max(|A|,D), the Cayley strict rotation (at most 2N forbidden s values) and the IID population bound I_p(D)/p^D all re-derive correctly. I recomputed the all-parameter rho=1 counterexample over F23 independently: D0 has roots 0,9,16 and every one of the 23 targets has at least two odd-multiplicity linear factors, while Q=13 is strictly perfect. The artifact confirms perfect 127/127 witnesses on both N127,K77 mixed inputs (1 and 15 trials, degrees 69 and 64, zero-including and strict). The Research Decision's summary of the previous experiment is inaccurate: common cosets were solved only above the threshold (K39 global scored 108 and 110 of 127), and it omits the unsolved r=3/r=4 mixed high-rate controls, which this quadratic attack cannot reach. The title drops that perfect witnesses exist only for two certified N127,K77 inputs and that the K39 inputs are not applicable.

claims.quote: Mixed Quadratic OPI: Perfect Classical Norm Witnesses And A Source Bound
claims.finding: Headline scope. A title-only reader sees 'Perfect Classical Norm Witnesses' for mixed quadratic OPI. The perfect witnesses exist only for the two saved N127,K77 inputs (and their strict siblings). The saved K39 inputs are NOT_APPLICABLE_DEGREE_BUDGET (sufficient K 70 and 65 > 39), the application is review pending, and no fixed-input frequency guarantee exists for the expanded pencil.

claims.quote: solved common cosets classically but left mixed high-rate controls at124/127 and122/127
claims.finding: Summary omission and overstatement. The previous experiment solved common cosets only when K>=(r-1)ceil(N/r): the N127,K39 global inputs scored 108/127 and 110/127 and remain unsolved. It also left the high-rate mixed controls r=3 N63,K46 (55/63, 56/63) and r=4 N32,K24 (28/32, 27/32) and N31,K16 seed 71 (30/31) unsolved. This quadratic norm attack does not apply to r=3/4, so 'solves BOTH' covers only two of the open mixed inputs.

claims.quote: The new attack solves BOTH saved N127,K77 mixed inputs perfectly, including strict nonzero variants
claims.finding: The artifact has four K77 results with status CLASSICAL_NATIVE_PERFECT_WITNESS and score 127 (include_zero True and False for each seed), using 1 and 15 trials with degrees 69 and 64 < 77. The orientation splits |A|=69,|B|=58 (D=58) and |A|=64,|B|=63 padded to D=64 match the stated D=58 and 64.

claims.quote: Thus a monic polynomial is a norm exactly when every odd-degree irreducible has even multiplicity.
claims.finding: Standard: an even-degree irreducible splits into conjugate factors g*bar(g) in F_(p^2)[X], and an odd-degree one stays inert, so its norm is its square. Because nu is a nonsquare, the leading terms of R^2-nu Z^2 cannot cancel, which forces deg R,Z<=D/2, so the degree budget K>max(|A|,D) is sufficient.

claims.quote: Thus NONE of the23 parameters is a norm, although OPI itself is easy.
claims.step: Try To Disprove The Pencil, Then Repair It
claims.finding: Independently recomputed with FLINT over F23. D0=V_A-V_B=16x(x+7)(x+14) has roots 0,16,9. For every lambda in F23, F0+V_B has at least two odd-multiplicity linear factors (23/23). Q=13 gives residue 13 (a square) on A and 17,14,5,7 (all nonsquares) on B, so the input is strictly perfect.

claims.quote: Therefore first-trial success is at least I_p(D)/p^D
claims.finding: Conditioned on the A shifts and on lambda,rho, interpolation is a bijection, so F/rho^2 is uniform monic of degree D. An irreducible of even degree D>=2 is a norm with no Fp root, so Cayley avoidance applies for p>2N. The 1/(2N) corollary also checks: D<=N and (1-2p^(-D/2))/D>=1/(2N). The scope (population, not per-input) is stated explicitly. I_11(2)=55 matches the 55/121 calibration.

summary: The hybrid bound (average uniform-sign TV <= sum_F m_i), the posterior-magnitude recursion, and the PSC degradation argument behind the upward-rounded certificate all check out. The live numbers match the artifacts: 16/78/361/1614 at N64..4096, 0.023431 for the rate-3/8 follow-up, and 0.0102208 with 65534 combinations and 1008335816 pair visits at N32768. The problem is scope: the half-rate certificate exists at exactly one length (N32768), and the half-rate targets FAIL (UNKNOWN) at every coarse length N<=4096. Yet the question/decision sentences say the pass removes the construction blocker for 'families' and for 'the stated half-rate family'. The decision also drops that the m_i/root-fidelity identity and the degradation certificate are review pending (the identity is numerically checked only at N2/N4).

claims.quote: The preceding hybrid argument gives average uniform-sign Gibbs TV at most 2 epsilon_F = sum_F m_i.
claims.finding: Re-derived: TV(P_U,Q_U)<=sum_F E|P(U_i|prefix)-1/2| = sum_F m_i/2 = epsilon_F. Averaging over uniform s (uniform J, since H_F has full rank) adds at most TV(P_UF,unif)<=epsilon_F, giving 2 epsilon_F. The artifact's TV upper equals twice frozen_prefix_bias_sum (for example N32768: denominators 4.15e34 vs 8.31e34).

claims.quote: The computed mean overlaps are therefore upper bounds on the true m_i.
claims.finding: The Gram-matrix factorization |psi(a)> -> |psi(d)>|psi(a/d)> for a<=d is an isometry, so rounding overlaps up and moving herald mass to overlap one are degradations. Polar plus/minus combinations preserve degradedness, and root fidelity is monotone under CPTP maps. The plus/minus magnitude recursion (ab; (a+b)/(1+ab), |a-b|/(1-ab) with weights (1+-ab)/2) matches the PSC check/variable combinations, which supports the identification of m_i with root fidelity.

claims.quote: The larger G=256,r=3,b=96 calculation succeeds at N32768, |F|=16384
claims.finding: polar_source_design_n32768_g256_p3.json gives uniform_sign_average_Gibbs_TV_upper = 424553765284920852120940002337825/41538374868278621028243970633760768 = 0.0102208 < 0.010221, with constraint_count 16384, channel_combinations 65534 and active_support_pair_visits 1008335816, as stated. The coarse table (16/64 at N64, 78/256, 361/1024, 1614/4096) and the rate-3/8 bound 0.0234306 also match polar_source_design.json.

claims.quote: This pass removes that blocker for concrete non-prefix families.
claims.finding: Headline scope. 'Families' is certified at exactly one half-rate length (N32768, G256). At N=16..4096 every half-rate target is UNKNOWN_AT_THIS_GRID_AND_LENGTH (uniform_sign_average_Gibbs_TV_upper=1). The certificate also rests on the review-pending degradation/duality derivation (local_degradation_and_hybrid_derivation_review_pending=true). Neither condition is kept in this sentence.

claims.quote: This finite result removes the missing public-set construction premise for the stated half-rate family.
claims.finding: One certified length is not a family. The premise in the preceding sampler note is epsilon_F->0 with a polynomial construction. A single N=32768 set with TV<=0.0102, alongside failed half-rate certification at all smaller lengths, does not establish it for a family. The next sentence's denial of an asymptotic convergence theorem partly concedes this.

claims.quote: the matching classical route is now constructive
claims.finding: This decision sentence drops two conditions stated elsewhere. The equivalence between the quantum SC criterion and m_i (root fidelity) is numerically checked only at N2/N4 and is cited rather than proved. The certificate covers average uniform signs at specific finite lengths, and no 32768-bit Gibbs draw has been executed. Arbitrary-sign and non-SC receivers are excluded elsewhere, but the review-pending status of the bound is not kept here.

summary: The hybrid TV bound, the uniform- and native-syndrome averages (<= epsilon_F+delta <= 2 epsilon_F), prefix exactness, and the Pinsker/Jensen entropy bound all re-derive correctly. The calibration rows match the artifact: N2 average 0.4, worst 0.72, native 18/125. I recomputed the N8 source biases exactly: {0,1,2,4} are the four smallest (1,2,4 tie at 0.08925), with sum 0.28369 matching frozen_prefix_bias_sum. The reversed CQ/source duality agrees in the artifact to about 7e-16. The follow-up header overstates what the later design note resolves: the premise here is epsilon_F->0 with a polynomial construction, but the follow-up certifies one half-rate length (N32768, TV<=0.010221) under a review-pending degradation proof, and its half-rate targets fail at all smaller lengths.

claims.quote: It resolves the missing public-set premise below for that finite family
claims.finding: The premise below is asymptotic: 'If the corresponding source set has epsilon_F->0 with a polynomial construction'. The follow-up artifact certifies a single half-rate length (N32768) with fixed TV 0.0102. Its half-rate targets at N=16..4096 are all UNKNOWN (TV upper 1), and its degradation certificate is flagged review pending. A single certified length does not resolve a premise about epsilon_F->0 along a family.

claims.quote: E_(uniform s) TV(Q_s,P_(U|U_F=s)) <= epsilon_F+delta <= 2 epsilon_F
claims.step: Average-Syndrome Guarantee, Not A Worst-Case Guarantee
claims.finding: Re-derived from the joint coupling: E_unif TV <= TV(Qjoint,P)+TV(P_UF,unif) <= epsilon_F+delta, and delta<=epsilon_F because Qjoint has a uniform U_F marginal. The N2 calibration checks out exactly: epsilon_F=2/5, average 2/5, native average 18/125, worst 18/25.

claims.quote: For a contiguous initial frozen prefix, however, the remaining chain is already conditioned on every constraint
claims.finding: When F is a prefix, sampling U_i from P(U_i|U_<i) for i after the prefix is exactly the chain rule for P(U|U_F=s). The artifact's prefix calibrations (N4 {0,1}, N8 {0,1,2}) have TV 0 for all syndromes.

claims.quote: Pinsker and Jensen give E|P(U_i=1|prefix)-1/2| <= sqrt((ln 2)/2 * (1-H(U_i|U_<i)))
claims.finding: |q-1/2| = TV(Bern(q),Bern(1/2)) <= sqrt(KL/2), with KL = ln2 (1-h(q)) in nats. Jensen moves the expectation inside the square root.

claims.quote: Hence the CQ information at i equals the source conditional entropy at N-1-i.
claims.step: Why This Is Relevant To The Quantum Proposal
claims.finding: The PSC overlap is (1-p)-p=1-2p=c. The artifact shows Holevo [0.4709,0.8671] vs source entropies [0.8671,0.4709], and root fidelities [0.65,0.4225] vs biases [0.4225,0.65], with reverse-index errors <=6.7e-16 at N2 and N4. The general identity rests on cited known duality (Renes) and is presented as such.

claims.quote: The last set selects the four smallest EXACT source prefix biases
claims.finding: Exact recomputation with p=7/40 and U=E F^{(x)3} gives m = 0.0159, 0.0893, 0.0893, 0.2980, 0.0893, 0.3156, 0.3509, 0.4791. The four smallest are {0,1,2,4}, with sum 14525010721/51200000000, which matches the artifact. The table values 0.00416611 and 0.05596208 match the artifact.
